findings.title: Batch authorization validates only the first payment
findings.problem: The service checks only `payments[0].tenant_id` before iterating over and refunding every captured payment returned by the unscoped batch lookup.
findings.reason: Payment IDs are tenant-local and `get_many` receives no tenant, so a returned batch can contain payments from different tenants. If the first payment belongs to the actor, every later payment bypasses ownership validation and reaches `record_refund`, enabling a cross-tenant refund and integrity violation.
findings.suggestion: Validate every payment's tenant before performing any refund, rejecting the whole batch if one does not belong to the actor. Also prefer a tenant-scoped repository lookup.

security.public_safe_summary: Batch authorization validates only the first payment

findings.title: Global refund idempotency keys can collide across tenants
findings.problem: The repository key omits the tenant even though idempotency keys use a global namespace and payment IDs are unique only within a tenant.
findings.reason: Distinct tenants can use the same client key for the same tenant-local payment ID, producing identical repository keys. The repository must then treat separate cross-tenant refund operations as the same idempotent operation, suppressing or misattributing a legitimate refund.
findings.suggestion: Include the tenant namespace in every repository key, such as `f"{actor.tenant_id}:{idempotency_key}:{payment.id}"`.

security.public_safe_summary: Global refund idempotency keys can collide across tenants

findings.title: Timestamp-only cursor cannot paginate through tied rows
findings.problem: The cursor retains only `created_at`, although the declared row ordering also uses `id` as a tie-breaker.
findings.reason: When more than one page of rows shares a timestamp, the next request cannot identify which tied row ended the previous page. A timestamp-only boundary must omit remaining tied rows, repeat returned rows, or fail to advance, so pagination is not stable or gap-free.
findings.suggestion: Store both `created_at` and payment ID in `Cursor` and pass the composite cursor to `page_before` so its continuation predicate matches `(created_at DESC, id DESC)`.
